description: An integer has sequential digits if each digit in the number is one more than the previous digit. Return a sorted list of all integers in the range [low, high] that have sequential digits.
intuition: There are very few sequential digit numbers (at most 36 total, like 12, 123, 1234, etc.). You can simply generate all of them by starting from each digit 1-9 and extending, then filter by the given range.
approach: Generate all possible sequential digit numbers. Starting digits range from 1 to 9, and for each starting digit, extend the sequence by appending the next digit. Collect those within [low, high] and sort.
jsWalkthrough:
Input: low = 100, high = 300

start=1: 1 -> 12 -> 123 (>= 100, push) -> 1234 (> 300, stop)
start=2: 2 -> 23 -> 234 (>= 100, push) -> 2345 (> 300, stop)
start=3: 3 -> 34 -> 345 (> 300, stop)
start=4..9: first 3-digit numbers all > 300, nothing added

result before sort = [123, 234]
After sort = [123, 234]
Return [123, 234]
explanation:
1. Try each starting digit from 1 to 9.
2. Build numbers by appending the next sequential digit (start+1, start+2, ...).
3. Stop when the number exceeds high or the next digit would exceed 9.
4. Collect numbers that fall within [low, high].
5. Sort the result since numbers from different starting digits may interleave.
timeComplexity: O(1) since there are at most 36 sequential digit numbers
hints: There are very few sequential digit numbers (at most 36). Can you enumerate all of them?
Start from each digit 1-9 and keep appending the next consecutive digit.
Filter the generated numbers by the [low, high] range.
